name: Engine Piston Assembly
description: Positioned multi-body capstone: the 86 mm family Engine Piston, its 22 mm wrist pin, and the Engine Connecting Rod hanging 17 degrees off the cylinder axis, composed as a three-body Compound (no joints).

steps.instruction: Build the Engine Piston in its working frame, crown up.

transcript.user_prompt: Start a piston assembly for the 86 mm bore engine. First build the piston exactly like the catalog Engine Piston, in its own frame: an 85.5 mm diameter body 62 mm tall with its skirt bottom on Z=0, three 3 mm ring grooves cut 4.5 mm deep with bottoms at Z=52, 46 and 40, the skirt hollowed to a 6 mm wall below Z=50 leaving a 12 mm crown, two 16 mm radius pin bosses on the Y axis at Z=24 spanning Y=14..38 and Y=-14..-38, a 22 mm wrist-pin bore straight through at Z=24, and a 1 mm chamfer on the crown edge.
transcript.assistant_message: I built the piston, matching the catalog Engine Piston dimension for dimension: 85.5 mm diameter, 62 mm tall, three ring grooves, hollowed skirt, pin bosses, the 22 mm pin bore at Z=24, and the 1 mm crown chamfer. It sits crown-up in the assembly frame, ready to receive the wrist pin.

steps.instruction: Slide the wrist pin through the piston's pin bore as a second positioned body.

transcript.user_prompt: Now add the wrist pin as a separate positioned body, not fused to the piston: an 84 mm long full-floating pin on the piston's pin axis (along Y at Z=24), 21.9 mm diameter so it sits in the 22 mm bore with 0.05 mm radial running clearance, spanning Y=-42 to Y=42 so its end faces sit just inside the skirt surface. Return the piston and pin together as a two-body compound.
transcript.assistant_message: I placed the 84 mm wrist pin through the bore on the Y axis at Z=24, its ends stopping 0.75 mm shy of the skirt surface. At 21.9 mm diameter it floats in the 22 mm bore with 0.05 mm radial clearance, so the assembly is now a compound of two disjoint bodies: piston and pin.

steps.instruction: Hang the connecting rod on the wrist pin at a 17 degree crank angle, completing the three-body assembly.

transcript.user_prompt: Finally hang the catalog Engine Connecting Rod on the wrist pin as a third body: build the rod in its own frame (145 mm centres, 22 mm thick, 45 mm big-end bore, 22 mm small-end bore, I-beam shank, cap-bolt bosses with M8 clearance holes), then position it so its small-end bore is coaxial with the pin at Z=24 — its 22 mm thickness centred in the 28 mm gap between the pin bosses — with the big end swung 17 degrees off the cylinder axis towards +X, hanging below the piston. Keep all three parts disjoint, positions only, no joints.
transcript.assistant_message: I built the connecting rod to the catalog dimensions and hung it on the wrist pin: small-end bore coaxial with the pin (0.05 mm radial clearance), thickness centred between the pin bosses with 3 mm a side, and the big end swung 17 degrees off the cylinder axis, its centre landing 145 mm down the rod axis at about (42.4, 0, -114.7). The result is a three-body compound — piston, pin, rod — positioned but unconstrained.
